title: Delta-CRL numbering: uint_to_u64, crl_number and base_crl_number are unpinned
description:
## Why

Delta-CRL application turns on two numbers: the delta's `deltaCRLIndicator`
(the base CRL number it updates) and the base's own `cRLNumber`. Nothing
pins how either is read.

## The survivors

    crl.rs:1357:5   replace uint_to_u64 -> Option<u64> with Some(0)
    crl.rs:1357:5   replace uint_to_u64 -> Option<u64> with Some(1)
    crl.rs:1358:16  replace > with == in uint_to_u64
    crl.rs:1358:16  replace > with >= in uint_to_u64
    crl.rs:1375:5   replace crl_number -> Option<Result<u64, der::Error>> with None
    crl.rs:1375:5   replace crl_number -> ... with Some(Ok(1))
    crl.rs:1414:5   replace base_crl_number -> ... with Some(Ok(0))
    crl.rs:1414:5   replace base_crl_number -> ... with Some(Ok(1))

`uint_to_u64` returning a constant makes every CRL number read as the same
value, so a delta pairs with any base. Its `b.len() > 8` guard decides
whether an oversize INTEGER is refused -- the rustdoc says a `CRLNumber`
above 2^64 "must not silently disable the staleness check", and `>=` would
refuse an eight-byte number that fits.

`crl_number -> None` means "this CRL has no cRLNumber", which is the
extension-absent signal; `base_crl_number -> Some(Ok(n))` claims a delta
indicator the CRL does not carry.

The existing `delta-crl-*` fixtures are a matching pair (base CRLNumber=1,
delta BaseCRLNumber=1) and `with_delta` already rejects a base supplied as a
delta, so the construction-time checks are covered. What is not covered is
the arithmetic that compares the two numbers.

## What a test needs

Fixtures with deliberately mismatched numbers: a delta whose BaseCRLNumber is
higher than the base's CRLNumber, one where it is lower, and a CRL number
encoded in nine bytes. `gen_delta_crl_fixtures.py` is the oracle for the
first two; the oversize one is raw INTEGER DER plus a re-sign, the way
`pkix-path/tests/fixtures/dup-ext/gen.py` does its surgery.

## Found by

The first pkix-revocation mutation sweep, 2026-11-27.
close_reason: All eight killed. tests/delta_crl_numbers.rs with fixtures/delta-crl-numbers/: 3-against-5 and 9-against-5 so neither direction of the comparison passes by coincidence, plus the eight-byte boundary (2^56 fits, 2^64 is a parse error rather than an absent number). The existing delta-crl-* pair is 1 against 1, which satisfies the comparison without distinguishing it from a constant.
